 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Atlanta Braves struck quickly in free agency Thursday, Nov. 12 to sign a key member of the Los Angeles Dodgers ' bullpen.
 Former closer Evan Phillips signed a three-year contract with Atlanta worth $35 million, with the right-hander set to make $11 million in the 2027 and 2028 seasons, and $13 million in 2029.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Phillips, 32, appeared in 31 games last season, going 3-2 with a 3.46 ERA (10 ER/26.0 IP) and 33 strikeouts. He made his season debut on July 7 after returning from Tommy John surgery, and compiled a 5.27 ERA (8 ER/13.2 IP) in his first 17 appearances of the season. In his final 14 games, from August 21 through the end of the season, he pitched to a 1.46 ERA (2 ER/12.1 IP) and fanned 19 batters.
 MORE: Former Dodgers pitcher immediately retires from MLB 
 Phillips also made five scoreless appearances for the Dodgers in the 2026 postseason. The Braves are counting on more of the same in 2027 from Phillips, who will join Robert Suarez to form a potent right-handed duo in the back of their bullpen.
 A two-time World Series champion (2024, 2025), Phillips is 19-14 with 47 career saves and a 3.37 ERA over 281 career appearances between Atlanta (2018), the Baltimore Orioles (2018-20), Tampa Bay Rays (2021) and Los Angeles (2021-26).
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Phillips saved 24 games in 2023, and 18 in 2024, before injuries and ineffectiveness forced him down the Dodgers' bullpen depth chart.
 MORE: Dodgers bring back Pedro Guerrero — not the All-Star — as coach 
 When healthy, however, Phillips' track record suggests a three-year contract could be worth the gamble. The Braves are facing the potential loss of veteran closer Raisel Iglesias in free agency, creating an obvious opening for Phillips — who's four years younger than Iglesias.
 The signing could also help the Braves transition pitching prospect Didier Fuentes to their rotation. The 21-year-old made all but one of his 58 appearances for the Braves in relief this season, going 7-2 with a 2.45 ERA.
